marker.description: Faint pink paint on the posterior shaft of the humerus.

main_question: What passes through the area painted pink?
main_answer: Radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
main_explanation: The pink paint indicates the radial groove (spiral groove) on the posterior aspect of the humeral shaft.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following is a common clinical sign of radial nerve injury at the level of the radial groove?
supporting_question.explanation: Injury to the radial nerve in the radial groove often results in paralysis of the extensors of the wrist and fingers, leading to a characteristic 'wrist drop'.

true_false.statement: The radial nerve is a terminal branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus.
true_false.explanation: The radial nerve originates from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus, receiving fibers from C5-T1.
